abstract: Dallas Fed economists Samuel Dodini and Tucker Smith (September 1, 2026) link occupation-level GenAI automation exposure, built from Anthropic's Claude-usage task measure mapped to O*NET, to Lightcast job postings in Texas. After ChatGPT's release, postings fell for occupations whose tasks GenAI can automate: about 5 percent for more- vs less-exposed positions (per 10 percentage points of automatable tasks, within industry) by end-2023 and about 8 percent by 2025 Q1. The decline is not driven by new AI-native firms or firm exit: a balanced panel of incumbent firms cut exposed postings 8-9 percent by early 2026, and more-exposed firms shifted the task mix of their ads away from automatable work. In aggregate, the authors estimate GenAI automation exposure reduced total Texas Lightcast postings by about 1.8 percent in 2024 and 2.6 percent in 2025, which is modest overall but concentrated on specific workers, especially new entrants, because online postings mostly require little experience. Two-thirds of Texas firms reported using AI in the May 2026 Texas Business Outlook Survey, up from 40 percent two years earlier.
keyFindings: Job postings fell 5 percent for more-exposed vs less-exposed positions by end-2023 and about 8 percent by 2025 Q1 (scaled to a 10-percentage-point difference in the share of automatable tasks, within industry, Texas).
Incumbent firms more exposed to AI cut postings about 5-6 percent by mid-2024 and 8-9 percent by early 2026, statistically indistinguishable from the occupation-industry results.
Firms whose pre-ChatGPT postings were 10 percent more automatable posted jobs with 2 percentage points fewer automatable tasks afterwards, a nearly 50 percent reduction relative to the mean.
GenAI automation exposure reduced total Texas Lightcast job postings by about 1.8 percent in 2024 and 2.6 percent in 2025.
Two-thirds of Texas firms surveyed in the May 2026 Texas Business Outlook Survey reported using AI, up from 40 percent two years prior.
Fewer than half of typical online job ads require more than two years of experience, so the posting decline likely falls disproportionately on new entrants.
methodology: Occupation exposure: Anthropic Economic Index task-level Claude usage mapped to O*NET tasks, read as the share of an occupation's tasks GenAI can automate. Outcome: quarterly Lightcast postings in Texas (220,000+ job boards and company sites). Event-study comparing more- vs less-exposed occupations within the same industry before and after November 2022; a balanced panel of firms present throughout, with exposure fixed on pre-ChatGPT postings. The aggregate effect combines estimated elasticities with AI usage rates, automation scores and Texas industry composition. A national occupation-industry re-estimate is reported as similar.
qualifiers: Tier 1: Federal Reserve Bank research publication. Caveats: postings measure labor demand, not employment; a posting pullback is not job loss. Texas only (national check described but not reported numerically). Lightcast underrepresents farming, construction, building maintenance and personal services. The exposure measure reflects Claude usage patterns, which skew toward software and writing tasks. The relative estimate is scaled per 10 percentage points of automatable tasks, not a high-vs-low contrast. The aggregate 1.8-2.6 percent figures are model-implied, not directly observed. The authors characterise the aggregate effect as modest.
